# AiroHub

> A collaborative 3D spray-paint studio that runs in a browser tab. Put a real
> 3D object on a big screen, and up to four phones become motion-tracked spray
> cans pointed at it. Everyone paints the same object at the same time. No
> install, no account, one six-character room code.

This file follows the llms.txt community convention (llmstxt.org). It is a
convention, not a web standard: nothing is obliged to read it, and nothing here
is authoritative over the pages themselves. It exists because AiroHub is a
client-rendered WebGL app whose interesting content lives in a JavaScript
bundle, and a plain-text pointer costs nothing.

## Pages

- https://airohub.netlify.app/ — the landing page and the entry point. Creates a
  studio (a room) or joins one with a code.
- https://airohub.netlify.app/how-it-works — the field guide. The long-form
  explanation of the studio, the phone controller, the three controller modes
  and the engineering underneath, plus a list of common questions.

## How it works, in one paragraph

Nobody streams pixels. A phone reads its own gyroscope about 40 times a second
and sends where it is aiming; the studio raycasts that aim onto the model and
composites the stroke into the model's own texture, so paint survives camera
moves, object swaps and a page reload. Every screen in the room rebuilds the
identical artwork from the same instructions. The transport is Supabase Realtime
broadcast and presence — there is no dedicated socket server.

## Not for indexing

/canvas/*, /controller/* and /admin* are live session surfaces behind throwaway
codes. They hold no durable content, they are disallowed in robots.txt, and they
are served with X-Robots-Tag: noindex.

## Requirements

A modern browser with WebGL. Free, no account, no install.
